description: Creates a short link to a registration page that counts its clicks and carries the tracking of its channel, so a pretty address goes into an invitation instead of a long one. Take it when you share a link and want to know what it brought. A host says: "Give me a short link for the newsletter, one per person if possible." It needs the session and the webinar, and the channel where the link will be shared. You can add a short topic word, create several links at once that differ by number, or let one link carry a form value for one person, for example who sent them. For several sources at once you get one link per source. It adds the link to the campaign's list and counts clicks from now on; nothing else changes. Side effect: it acts on your connected WordPress site; nothing else is touched. Words hosts use: short link, tracking link, link for the newsletter, click count

count.description: How many links at once, 1 to 10. Default 1.

fields.description: Form values the link should fill in for the participant, e.g. {"wi_8": "Anna"} for a hidden field. One link per person when each carries its own value.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

sources.description: Several sources in one call, one link per entry.

count.description: How many links for this source, 1 to 10.

fields.description: Form values this link should carry.

label.description: A name for this source, e.g. the group it goes into.

word.description: A short topic word for this link.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

word.description: A short topic word of 3 to 10 letters for the address, invented to fit the topic.

name: wi_create_webinar_link
title: Create a short tracking link for a webinar
